name: Silkie

attributes.attribute: untidied rooms if nothing was left to clean
harvest goddess sometimes linked to Silkie

sources: Briggs, Katherine M. An Encyclopedia of Fairies: Hobgoblins, Brownies, Bogies, and Other Supernatural Creatures. New York: Pantheon Books, 1976, 364–365.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Silkie is a Scottish house-goddess. She takes her name from the silk clothing she wore. She entered homes to tidy what lay out of place. A home kept too neat was as bad as a home left loose. If she found no work to do, she untidied the rooms. Some writers link her with the harvest goddess Sele. Others place her with the fairy folk called the Silly Witches. Some see her as a form of the brownie. The name silkie, or selkie, also names the human-looking seal race. The tale shifts between the two readings across the isles.
